info.bio:
Thomas Andrew Dorsey (1 de julio de 1899, Villa Rica, Georgia - 23 de enero de 1993, Chicago), denominado "El padre de la música gospel", fue además "Georgia Tom", alias por el que fue conocido en sus primeros años como pianista de blues.

Dorsey fue el director musical de la 'Pilgrim Baptist Church' de Chicago desde 1932 hasta los últimos años de la década de 1970. Su composición más famosa, "Take My Hand, Precious Lord", fue interpretada por Mahalia Jackson siendo además la favorita de Martin Luther King; otra de sus composiciones

scenes.name: Antecedentes (1892-1950)
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: Antes del rock'n'roll: Tin Pan Alley, los primeros discos de blues (Mamie Smith) y de «old-time music», el yodel de Jimmie Rodgers, el crooning de Bing Crosby, el boogie-woogie, el jump blues de Louis Jordan (nacimiento de facto del rhythm'n'blues), la guitarra jazzística de T-Bone Walker, Woody Guthrie como primer gran cantautor y la exótica de Les Baxter. En paralelo, la vanguardia clásica (Russolo, Satie, Varèse, Cage, Schaeffer) anticipa el ruido, el ambient y la electrónica.

podcast.title: Inventor of Gospel Music
podcast.body: Thomas Dorsey is largely credited with inventing gospel music as it is known today, around 1930. He combined themes and melodies from traditional Christian hymns with the feel of blues and jazz, incorporating popular music idioms into the genre. "gospel music as we know it basically was invented by Thomas Dorsey."

podcast.title: Personal Struggle and Career Shift
podcast.body: Dorsey, a blues and jazz musician (also known as Georgia Tom), experienced multiple breakdowns due to the conflict between his faith and his secular music career. At one point, he was unable to play the piano on stage with Marraini. This led him to eventually focus entirely on making religious music, though he maintained parallel careers for a while. "He did this, because he was so torn between his faith and his work as a blues musician, that he had multiple breakdowns, at one point finding himself on stage with Marraini, and completely unable to move his fingers to play the piano."

podcast.title: Pioneer of New Gospel Music
podcast.body: Thomas Dorsey was a pivotal figure in Chicago, spearheading the creation of a new, revolutionary form of gospel music during the 1940s, influencing young artists like Sam Cooke. "Chicago which...was the city where a whole new form of gospel music was being created at that point, spearheaded by Thomas Dorsey."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
srcs.episode: Episode Sixty: "You Send Me" by Sam Cooke

podcast.title: Revolutionary Musician
podcast.body: Dorsey is described as a man who revolutionized music multiple times over, through his foundational work in hocombe blues with Tampa Red and his invention of modern gospel music. "That's one man, a man who personally revolutionized music multiple times over, writing about his own personal grief, and creating something that stands as great art, without having to be patronised or given special consideration."
